verses.1: For this man was Melchisedec, king of Salem, priest of the god who is supreme. He met Abraham while he was being rescued from the slaughter of kings. He blessed him.
verses.2: Abram was also chosen as the twelfth in all of them. First, he was interpreted as a king of justice. Later, he became a king of peace. He is indeed a king of peace.
verses.3: He who is without beginning, without end, and without honor; who has neither a beginning in days nor an end in life; who is banished by the Son of God; remains as a priest during the periods of waiting.
verses.4: Consider this person as a “pet” or treasure, given that he was given ten Abrahams by the patriarch.
verses.5: And those who receive the priestly office from the descendants of Levi are commanded by law to serve the people according to that law. This applies to their brothers as well. Just as Abraham was removed from his position as priest.
verses.6: But the one who wasn’t of their age chose Abraham as his successor. He also entrusted the task of carrying out these messages to him.
verses.7: However, in cases of complete disagreement, the lesser one is favored by the more powerful.
verses.8: And yet, twelve people die each time. But those who are reported to be alive still live.
verses.9: And as the saying goes, because Abraham and Levi received twelve men, they were also called “twelve”.
verses.10: For he was still in his father’s house when Melchisedek joined him there.
verses.11: If then the end was achieved through the worship of Leuitica, then why should the people still resist having a priest according to the order of Melchizedek? Why not follow the order of Aaron instead?
verses.12: It is forced and by law that the priestly office is taken away from someone.
verses.13: For it is said that someone from another tribe took part in this sacrifice, while no one from his own tribe did so.
verses.14: It is clear that it was from Judah that our Lord was sent. Moses never spoke about any restrictions regarding the tribe of priests.
verses.15: And it’s even more obvious that, according to the similarity between Melchisedec and other priests, another priest is not worthy of being considered a priest at all.
verses.16: Who acted not according to the law of flesh’s commandment, but according to the power of life’s force.
verses.17: It is proved that you, priest, were in charge of the affairs during the reign of Melchisedek.
verses.18: For the act of detestation indeed occurs when an order is given, due to its own weakness and usefulness.
verses.19: For nothing was accomplished by this law; rather, it only created a false hope that led us to trust in God.
verses.20: And as long as there is no breach of vows (for those who have breached their vows, they have become priests).
verses.21: But after making the oath, he spoke to him. “O Lord, I will not be punished. You, priest, will remain in your position until the end of time.”
verses.22: By such a restrictive covenant, Jesus became a bondman.
verses.23: And those who have become priests in the past will still remain priestly because of their deaths.
verses.24: But because it remains in the state of being “in the wilderness,” it lacks the dignity that is associated with holiness.
verses.25: Thus, it can also protect those who approach God through it, enabling them to live forever in His service.
verses.26: For he was indeed our archbishop, a man of noble character, upright and honorable, free from sin, and appointed by God himself. He also became the most high among all those who were in heaven.
verses.27: He who has no need to offer sacrifices every day, like the high priests, who once offered sacrifices for their own sins. Then, he also offered sacrifices for the sins of the people. (This was something he did in order to save himself from punishment.)
verses.28: For the law made it necessary for people to become priests, even when they were sick. But the concept of celibacy became a result of that law, and it was completely abolished over time.
